en.html:
Consideration, in the Prince's way. Probably that was what he meant.
It meant nothing beyond that, because the problem was elsewhere. To compel somebody to die—to erase a person. That enormous fact was the problem.

Where the responsibility lay was a secondary matter.
And even on that matter, I could not accept what the Prince was saying.

In an organization, naturally the one giving an order took responsibility for the act. But if the recipient could choose yes or no, responsibility for that decision was his as well.
Act as though I knew nothing? That was asking the impossible.

It would be my decision, without question, and my responsibility.
Whether to kill the Lord General, and one more person close to me who was probably innocent.

............Whichever way I considered it, the conclusion went one way only.

それは親王なりの気遣いではあったのだろう。
　そしてそれ以上の意味は無かった。何故ならば事の
問題はそこではない。誰かに死を強いる――消してし
まうという一大事実こそが問題だ。

　責任の所在など二次的な案件に過ぎない。
　その上でしかも、舞殿宮の言い分は俺には受け入れ
られないものだった。

　組織において行動の責任を命令した人間が負うのは
当然だが、命令された者とて、諾否の選択を許されて
いたならその決断に責任を負わねばならない。
　知らぬ顔を決め込めというのは無理な話だ。

　俺は間違いなく俺の責任において、決断することに
なる。
　大将領ともう一人、俺の身近の、罪も無かろう人間
を殺めるか否かを。

　…………どう検討しても、結論は一途を辿った。

en.html:
舞殿宮"Kageaki...?"
Chief"Control yourself. ...Sit."
Kageaki"I have not forgotten...! Two years ago, that promise was made."
Kageaki"When everything was over, you would bring me to trial and have me executed!"
Chief"............"
Kageaki"After all this, you mean to go back on it...?"
Chief"Without that promise then, would you have retained your self-control?"
Kageaki"So... words only!? That is what it was!?"
Chief"There is no crime for which you must answer. His Highness has said as much."
Chief"Everything you have done since coming here was with my approval and His Highness's. Where guilt and responsibility lie, there is no doubt."
Kageaki"That is not so...!"
Chief"It is. That is why・・・ I permitted your actions."
Chief"Had I thought myself unable to bear the responsibility, I would never have let you act. Surely that much is obvious?"
Kageaki"I do not recall entrusting my responsibility to another man."
Chief"Recall it or do not. By the world's principles, that is how it stands. Go to court as you wish; the judgment will be the same."
Chief"Guilt and responsibility belong first not to the person made to act・・・・・, but to the person who made them act・・・・."

Chief"Nor Silver Star. If you can go no further, I will take over. Muramasa as well."

Kageaki"Mujhe saza chahiye! I want condemnationjudgment—the due return for the evil I have done!"

Kageaki"Have me put to death. That————is justice, is it not!!"
Chief"............"
舞殿宮"Kageaki... is dying what you want...?"
Kageaki"No, Your Highness."

I shook my head at the question from behind the screen.
Death—what I had seen so often, what I had so often forced upon others—coming to me instead. The very thought was horrifying beyond measure.

My skin crawled; stomach acid <ruby>pressed<rt>rose</rt></ruby> upwards.

舞殿宮"Then, surely—"
Kageaki"Precisely for that reason, I ought to die. Your Highness, Prince Maidono."
Kageaki"To die because one wants death is only an escape into comfort. Where is the punishment in it? It is simply suicide: giving up on atonement."
Kageaki"I loathe death more than anything. Yet that very death, I have imposed upon so many others. If a death penalty is to be given, it must be to such a man."

en.html:
Kageaki"Let justice be carried out! Sentence me to death, and I shall weep and scream like the wretch I am. I shall beg for mercy, cry apologies far too late to the people I have killed—"
Kageaki"Until I mount the gallows, every moment I shall spend writhing in anguish. Your Highness, please!"
Kageaki"Here, in the name of Prince Haruhiro of Maidono, promise that such will be the end given to Kageaki Minato...!"
舞殿宮"..."
舞殿宮"No... that will not do."
Kageaki"Your Highness!"
舞殿宮"You cannot put the guilt aside, Kageaki. All right, perhaps asking you to make a clean break is asking too much. But dying over it—what does that accomplish?"
舞殿宮"Death will not make amends for anything... will it?"
Kageaki"That is the living's reasoning! There is no making amends to the dead in the first place. They cannot speak any longer. They cannot desire anything."
Kageaki"At least impose the equivalent punishment. Make it equal・・. Nothing else can be done."
舞殿宮"............"
舞殿宮"It isn't that I don't understand what you are saying. ...Even so, no."
舞殿宮"You must not die. That, I cannot agree to."
Kageaki"...Chief!"
Chief"If you think of the dead, live in their place and do something. Your dying means nothing. Do something, and meaning will come of it."
Kageaki"...!!"

For a crime, there ought to be a punishment equal to its weight. Was that not the principle of the human world? Was that not its order? My foster mother.◆ Yuhi Nitta.◆ Fuki.¦ Funa... en.text:
No.
They did not understand.

Neither of them understood a thing.

Meaning was not the question.
Much lesslet alone was making amends.

Crime and punishment. That alone.
For a crime, there ought to be a punishment equal to its weight.

Was that not the principle of the human world?
Was that not its order?

My foster mother.◆
Yuhi Nitta.◆
Fuki.¦
Funa...

If I could kill those people and not even be punished,
what had they lived rightly for・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・!?

ja.html: 駄目だ。 　わかっていない。 　この二人は何もわかっていない。 　意味がどうこうという問題ではないのだ。 　況いわんや償いの問題でもない。 　ただ、罪と罰の問題なのだ。 　罪にはその重さに相当する罰が与えられて然るべき なのだ。 　それが人の世の原理。 　人の世の秩序ではないのか。 　養母。◆ 　新田雄飛。◆ 　ふき。¦ ふな…… 　あの人々を殺した俺が罰せられもしないなら、 　彼らは何のために正しく生きたのだ・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・!?
ja.text:
駄目だ。
　わかっていない。

　この二人は何もわかっていない。

　意味がどうこうという問題ではないのだ。
　況いわんや償いの問題でもない。

　ただ、罪と罰の問題なのだ。
　罪にはその重さに相当する罰が与えられて然るべき
なのだ。

　それが人の世の原理。
　人の世の秩序ではないのか。

　養母。◆
　新田雄飛。◆
　ふき。¦
ふな……

　あの人々を殺した俺が罰せられもしないなら、
　彼らは何のために正しく生きたのだ・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・・!?
